name: Spa Valley
tagline: The colonnades along the Tepla, where the town's whole idea lives
description: The narrow valley following the Tepla river, lined with colonnades, grand hotels and the pastel facades that make the postcards. The Vridlo geyser hall, the drinking springs and the walking paths up into the woods all start here. It is beautiful, expensive and almost entirely given over to the spa business.
bestFor: Stays built around the springs, the concerts and walking straight into the woods
pros: Colonnades, springs and forest paths at the door
The most beautiful streets in the town by far
Restaurants, spas and the theatre all within a short walk
cons: The highest prices in the town for everything
Crowded with day visitors and coach groups
Almost no ordinary shops or supermarkets

name: Dolni Brana and the Lower Town
tagline: Where residents actually shop, ten minutes below the springs
description: The commercial part of Karlovy Vary at the lower end of the valley around the main bus and rail connections, with supermarkets, banks, offices and ordinary restaurants. It is far less picturesque than the spa quarter and it is where daily life happens, at prices set for people who live here.
bestFor: Longer stays that need a supermarket more often than a colonnade
pros: Full range of everyday shopping and services
Prices set for residents rather than visitors
Bus and train connections in both directions
cons: Plain, and in places genuinely drab
Fifteen minutes on foot to the spa quarter

name: Westend
tagline: Villa quarter on the western slope, quiet and green
description: The hillside district above the spa valley to the west, built as villas for wealthy visitors in the late nineteenth century and still largely residential. Steep streets, mature trees, and a short but uphill walk down to the colonnades. It is the pleasantest place in town to actually live.
bestFor: Quiet stays with space and trees, and a walk down to the springs
pros: Ten minutes downhill to the spa quarter
cons: No shops or restaurants of its own

name: Ruzovy Vrch and Tuhnice
tagline: The residential districts on the Ohre, cheapest in the town
description: The everyday districts along the Ohre river below the spa valley, a mix of interwar apartment buildings and later blocks with local shops, schools and the sports hall. Rents here are a fraction of the spa quarter and the buses run frequently, which makes it the practical choice for a longer stay.
bestFor: Longer stays where the rent matters more than the address
pros: The lowest rents in Karlovy Vary
River path along the Ohre for running
cons: Mixed and sometimes tired housing stock

name: Brezova and the Slavkov Forest Edge
tagline: The southern approach, forest on three sides
description: The southern edge of town where the valley narrows and the Slavkov Forest protected area begins, with the Diana lookout above and walking trails leading straight out from the last houses. Accommodation is scattered and mostly houses. It is a genuinely quiet base with the town twenty minutes downstream.
bestFor: Stays where the walking paths matter more than the shops
pros: Forest trails and the Diana lookout on the doorstep
Very quiet with the best air in the town
Cheaper than anything in the valley
cons: Twenty to twenty-five minutes to the centre
